transcript:
Agent: Thanks for calling, how can I help?
Customer: I was charged twice for my June subscription.
Agent: I'm sorry about that. Let me check your account. I can see two charges of $29 on June 3rd. I'll refund one now.
Customer: Great, how long will it take?
Agent: It should appear in 3 to 5 business days. You'll get an email confirmation.
Customer: Okay, thanks, that's a relief.
label_notes: Refund was issued on the call; the refund posting and confirmation email are automatic, so no follow-up.

transcript:
Customer: The app keeps crashing when I open the photo gallery.
Agent: Which version are you on?
Customer: 4.2.1, on Android 14.
Agent: Thanks. Please clear the app cache and try again.
Customer: I did that, still crashing. This is so frustrating.
Agent: I understand. I've escalated this to our engineering team. They'll contact you within two days.
Customer: Fine. Two days, then.

Customer: I'm locked out of my account.
Agent: I can help with that. Can you confirm the email on the account?
Customer: It's j.m****@example.com. Sorry, that's the masked one, the full one is on file.
Agent: No problem, I've sent a reset link to the email on file.
Customer: Got it, I just logged in. Thanks, that worked.
Agent: Glad to help. Have a good day.

Customer: My order from last week still hasn't arrived. The tracking hasn't moved in five days.
Agent: I'm sorry. I see the package is held at a regional depot. I'm filing a trace request with the carrier.
Customer: How long does that take?
Agent: Usually 48 hours. If nothing turns up, we'll send a replacement at no cost. I'll email you the case number.
Customer: Okay. I'll wait for the email.

Customer: I want to cancel my premium plan.
Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. Would a 30 percent discount for three months change your mind?
Customer: No, I've already decided. Just cancel it.
Agent: Understood. Your plan will end at the close of the billing period on July 31.
Customer: Fine.

Customer: My card was declined. Can you check it?
Agent: Sure, please read me the card number.
Customer: It's 4111 1111 1111 1111, expiry 09/28, CVV 123.
Agent: Thank you. The card issuer is blocking the transaction. Please try a different card or contact your bank.
Customer: Ugh, okay. I'll call the bank.
Agent: Is there anything else?
Customer: No, that's all.

Customer: Hi, does your software support exporting to CSV?
Agent: Yes, go to Reports, then click Export and choose CSV.
Customer: Found it. Perfect.
Agent: Anything else I can help with?
Customer: No, thanks.
label_notes: How-to question about an existing feature; nothing is broken, so 'other' rather than 'technical'.

transcript:
Customer: I received the blue jacket but I ordered the black one.
Agent: I'm sorry about that. I'll send a return label and ship the black one out today.
Customer: My address is 42 Maple Street, Springfield, and my phone is 555-0142.
Agent: Got it, I've updated the address. You'll get a return label by email within an hour.
Customer: Great, thank you.
label_notes: Borderline: the agent commits to shipping the replacement today but the transcript never confirms it shipped. Labeled resolved; the model consistently reads it as unresolved, which is defensible. The customer must still return the wrong jacket, so follow-up.

transcript:
Customer: Why did my bill go from $10 to $12 this month?
Agent: Our standard plan price changed on March 1st. We emailed all customers about it in January.
Customer: I must have missed that. Is there anything cheaper?
Agent: The annual plan works out to $10 a month if you pay yearly, but the monthly plan is now $12.
Customer: Okay, I'll stay on monthly. I understand now.

Customer: Your dashboard keeps showing an error 500. I can't get any work done.
Agent: I'm sorry. We have a service outage affecting dashboards right now. Our engineers are working on it and expect it fixed within two hours.
Customer: Is there anything I can do in the meantime?
Agent: Unfortunately not. Your data is safe; it's only the dashboard that's down.
Customer: Fine, I'll wait. But this is the second outage this month.
label_notes: The fix depends on the engineering team, so unresolved with follow-up.

transcript:
Customer: I'd like to change the email on my account.
Agent: Sure. What's the new address?
Customer: priya.n@example.com
Agent: Thanks. Done, your account email is now priya.n@example.com.
Customer: Perfect, thank you.
label_notes: Full unmasked email address counts as personal data.

transcript:
Customer: I'd like to cancel. It's just too expensive for me right now.
Agent: I understand. I can offer you 50 percent off for the next three months if you'd like to stay.
Customer: Oh, really? Okay, that works. Let's do that.
Agent: Great, the discount is applied starting with your next bill.
Customer: Thanks, I appreciate it.

Customer: My lamp arrived with the base cracked.
Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. Could you email photos of the damage and the box to our support address? Once we have them we can approve a replacement.
Customer: Okay, I'll take pictures tonight.
Agent: Thank you. I've noted the case on your order.
label_notes: Replacement depends on the customer sending photos, so unresolved with follow-up.

transcript:
Customer: I was charged a late fee but I paid on time.
Agent: Let me verify your account. What are the last four digits of the card on file?
Customer: It ends in 4821.
Agent: Thank you. I see your payment posted a day late because of a bank holiday. I've removed the $5 late fee.
Customer: Great, thanks so much.
label_notes: Last four digits only is partial, so not personal data.

transcript:
Customer: When I click Download Invoice in Safari, nothing happens.
Agent: That usually means Safari is blocking the pop-up. Can you open Safari settings, go to Websites, then Pop-up Windows, and allow our site?
Customer: Okay... done. Let me try again. Yes, it downloaded!
Agent: Great.
Customer: Thanks, that was easy.

Customer: My account got locked after too many login attempts.
Agent: I can unlock it after verifying your identity. Can you confirm your date of birth?
Customer: March 3rd, 1990.
Agent: Thank you, that matches. Your account is unlocked now.
Customer: Thank you!

Customer: Do you offer a student discount?
Agent: We don't have a student discount at the moment. The annual plan is our lowest price, at about 15 percent off monthly.
Customer: Hm, that's a bit disappointing. Okay, thanks for letting me know.
label_notes: Question fully answered on the call, so resolved even though the answer was no.

transcript:
Customer: I just placed an order but I need it sent to my new place.
Agent: No problem, it hasn't shipped yet. What's the new address?
Customer: 18 Oak Avenue, Portland.
Agent: Updated. Your order will go to 18 Oak Avenue, Portland.
Customer: Great, thank you.

Customer: I want a refund for my annual plan. I've barely used it.
Agent: I'm sorry, but our policy only allows refunds within 30 days of purchase, and your plan started eight months ago.
Customer: That's ridiculous. Can't you make an exception?
Agent: I'm afraid I can't. I can cancel auto-renewal so you're not charged next year.
Customer: Don't bother. I'm going to dispute the charge with my bank.

Customer: My calendar stopped syncing between my phone and laptop.
Agent: Let's try signing out of the app on your phone and signing back in.
Customer: Okay, signed back in... the events are showing up now.
Agent: Great, sync is working again.
Customer: Awesome, thanks!

Customer: I got a new phone and now I can't get my two-factor codes.
Agent: For security, we need to verify your identity before resetting two-factor. I've texted you a secure link. Please upload a photo of your ID there, and we'll reset it within 24 hours.
Customer: Okay, I'll do that this afternoon.
Agent: Thank you for your patience.

Customer: My package was supposed to arrive yesterday.
Agent: Let me look. It's been delayed by a storm in the carrier's hub, but it's moving again and is now scheduled for Thursday.
Customer: Okay, as long as it's on the way.
Agent: It is. You'll get tracking updates by email.
Customer: Alright, thanks.

Customer: Cancel my subscription. Your service has been terrible.
Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. I've cancelled it; you won't be charged again.
Customer: Good. I should have done this months ago.

Customer: I'd like to set up a payment plan for my overdue balance.
Agent: Sure, I can help with that.
Customer: Do you need my social? It's 123-45-6789.
Agent: We don't need that, but thank you. I've set up three monthly payments of $40, charged automatically to your card on file.
Customer: Great, thanks for setting that up.

Caller: Hi, I run a small IT consultancy and I'm interested in reselling your product.
Agent: Thanks for your interest. I'll pass your details to our partnerships team. They'll email you within a week.
Caller: Sounds good.

Customer: After the last update, all my notes from this week are gone.
Agent: I'm really sorry. I can't restore them from here, so I'm escalating this to our tier 2 team. They'll call you back today.
Customer: You can reach me at 555-0199. Please hurry, those notes were for work.
Agent: I've added that to the ticket.

Customer: My package was delivered to my old address. I forgot to update it.
Agent: I'm sorry. Since it's already delivered, we can't redirect it. You'll need to contact the carrier or the current residents at that address.
Customer: Great. That's going to be a pain.

Customer: My promo code didn't apply at checkout.
Agent: Sorry about that. I've added a $15 credit to your account to cover it. It'll apply to your next bill.
Customer: Oh nice, thank you!

Customer: How do I change my display name?
Agent: I can do it for you. What would you like it to be?
Customer: Sam K.
Agent: Done, your display name is now Sam K.
Customer: Thanks!

Customer: My card expired and my payment failed. I want to add a new one.
Agent: Sure, go ahead with the card number.
Customer: 5500 0000 0000 0004, expiry 11/29.
Agent: Thank you. The card is updated and your payment went through.
Customer: Perfect, thanks.

Customer: I returned my headphones two weeks ago. Where's my refund?
Agent: Your return arrived at our warehouse yesterday. Our team inspects returns within 3 to 5 days, and the refund is issued once the inspection is done.
Customer: Okay, so I just wait?
Agent: That's right.
Customer: Fine.
label_notes: The customer is asking about a refund, which the definitions put under billing (originally mislabeled as shipping; corrected because the label contradicted the written definition, not to match the model). The refund depends on the warehouse team inspecting the return, which is a person acting, not an automatic process.

transcript:
Customer: This is the third time your app has crashed while I'm trying to pay! I'm sick of it!
Agent: I'm sorry. Which version are you on?
Customer: I don't know, whatever it is.
Agent: There was a payment bug in older versions. Could you update the app from the store and try again?
Customer: Okay... updated. It worked this time. Wow, thank you so much, sorry for yelling.
Agent: No problem at all.
label_notes: Sentiment is judged at the end of the call.
